main.question_text: Which command initializes a brand-new Git repository in the current folder?
main.explanation: git init creates the .git metadata directory and begins tracking the current folder as a Git repository.

main.question_text: Which command shows the working tree status, staged files, and untracked files?
main.explanation: git status displays paths that have differences between the index file and the current HEAD commit.

main.question_text: Which command stages all modified and deleted files in the entire working directory?
main.explanation: git add -A (or git add --all) stages new, modified, and deleted files throughout the repository.

main.question_text: Which command creates a new branch named 'feature-login' without switching to it?
main.explanation: git branch <name> creates the branch pointer at HEAD without moving the current HEAD pointer.

main.question_text: Which modern command switches your working directory to an existing branch named 'dev'?
main.explanation: git switch was introduced in Git 2.23 as the clean, dedicated command for switching branches.

main.question_text: You are on branch 'main'. Which command incorporates all commits from 'feature' into 'main'?
main.explanation: git merge <branch> joins the specified branch's history into the current active branch.

main.question_text: Which command aborts an ongoing merge conflict and restores the working tree to pre-merge state?
main.explanation: git merge --abort safely cleans up conflicts and resets HEAD to where it was before the merge began.

main.question_text: Which command downloads a copy of an existing remote repository onto your local computer?
main.explanation: git clone copies the remote repository, sets up tracking branches, and checks out the default branch.

main.question_text: What is the difference between 'git fetch' and 'git pull'?
main.option_a: git fetch downloads objects without merging; git pull fetches and merges into the current branch
main.option_b: git fetch works over SSH while git pull works only over HTTPS
main.option_c: git pull only updates tags while git fetch updates code files
main.option_d: There is no difference; they are aliases for the same underlying operation
main.explanation: git pull is essentially a shortcut for running git fetch followed by git merge FETCH_HEAD.

main.question_text: Which command uploads a new local branch 'experiment' and configures upstream tracking to origin?
main.explanation: The -u (or --set-upstream) flag links the local branch to the remote branch on origin for future git pull/push.

main.question_text: Which command unstages a file 'app.js' from the staging area without discarding working edits?
main.explanation: git restore --staged removes the specified file from the index while keeping modifications in the working tree.

main.question_text: You want to create a new commit that exactly inverts the changes of a faulty commit. Which command should you use?
main.explanation: git revert safely produces a new commit that records the exact inverse of the targeted commit.

main.question_text: You need to undo the last commit while keeping all its modified files in the staging area. What is the command?
main.explanation: git reset --soft moves HEAD back one commit without touching the index or working tree.

main.question_text: You accidentally ran 'git reset --hard' and lost unpushed commits. Where can you find their commit hashes?
main.explanation: git reflog records every update to the tip of branches and HEAD, allowing recovery of lost commits.

main.question_text: Which command applies the exact changes introduced by commit 'a1b2c3d' from another branch onto your branch?
main.explanation: git cherry-pick applies the changes recorded by an existing commit to your current branch as a new commit.
